tagline: Small towns and a county courthouse beside the low-gradient James River
intro: The James River drains a flat lowland between the Missouri Coteau and Coteau des Prairies. Its fall of approximately five inches per mile sometimes allows high tributary flows to push water upstream for several miles. That reversal happens most frequently north of Huron, South Dakota.

In LaMoure County, Grand Rapids took its name from rapids in the James. Its post office opened in 1880; LaMoure was founded two years later, and Dickey in 1885. LaMoure became the setting for a Beaux Arts courthouse built in 1907.

Dickey and Grand Rapids are LaMoure County communities. LaMoure lies on the James River and serves as the county seat. Its courthouse dome has a metal covering and bull’s-eye windows, supported by an octagonal tower.

moments.title: Dickey
moments.text: Dickey was founded in 1885 and named for George H. Dickey. The 2020 census counted 42 residents in this LaMoure County city, the same population recorded in 2010.

moments.title: Grand Rapids
moments.text: Grand Rapids takes its name from rapids in the James River. A post office opened here in 1880 and operated until 1966. Grand Rapids is an unincorporated community in LaMoure County.

moments.title: LaMoure
moments.text: A metal-covered dome with bull’s-eye windows crowns LaMoure County’s courthouse. Below it, an octagonal tower carries columns and arched windows; four large columns mark the front facade. Buechner & Orth designed the Beaux Arts building, constructed in 1907. LaMoure itself was founded in 1882 and named for territorial legislator Judson LaMoure. The James River city is the county seat, and its courthouse entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.
moments.notice: Look for the courthouse dome’s bull’s-eye windows and ball finial.
